name: Low-Power Scooter
description: A self-propelled vehicle designed primarily for the roadways, with no more than three wheels on the ground, no manual clutch and, if electric, a motor of no more than 4,476 watts. An e-bike whose motor exceeds 750 watts, or a seated electric two-wheeler without working pedals, is a low-power scooter when it stays within those limits. Defined by Colorado Revised Statutes §42-1-102(48.5).

restrictions.rule: No more than three wheels on the ground, no manual clutch, and designed primarily for use on the roadways
Its electric motor is rated at no more than 4,476 W; the statute sets no top speed
A toy vehicle, bicycle, electrical assisted bicycle, electric scooter or wheelchair is not a low-power scooter; one over 4,476 W or with a manual clutch is a motorcycle
Its operator needs a valid driver's license or minor driver's license, but no motorcycle endorsement
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a motorcycle helmet meeting FMVSS 218
Riders and passengers must wear goggles or eyeglasses with safety glass or plastic lenses, unless their helmet has eye protection
Registered with the DMV for three years at a time, with a number decal fixed to its frame
Can only be registered or renewed with a complying motor vehicle insurance policy in force
Barred from interstates (except where bicycles may ride), limited-access state highways, and sidewalks unless specifically designated
May ride on roadways and in the bicycle lanes within them, as close to the right side as practicable and no more than two abreast
Ridden only on its permanent seat, carrying no more people than it is designed for
Not a motor vehicle except under the DUI, license-suspension, vehicular-homicide and habitual-offender laws
